question: Does averaging the existing inner CNN/STT models with each outer refit model lower the person-equal left/right GDI MAE of the current best mean-difference ensemble?
members: Per outer fold f and family (CNN, STT): the outer refit model plus the four inner models j != f. Inner model (f,j) was trained without fold f and fold j people.
member_prediction: Mean of window predictions per recording and side, then that model's own OLS calibration fitted only on its training recordings (reused from robust-aggregation692 cache, mean aggregator).
exclusion_rule: Drop a member whose uncalibrated mean-aggregated predictions on its own training recordings have standard deviation < 0.01 GDI points on either side. Uses training data only.
bagging: Equal-weight mean of the remaining members, separately for CNN and STT.
ensemble: Keep mean-difference692 fold weights (cnn_weight, fraction) and the outer bilateral STT difference; no refitting and no new selection.
primary_comparison: bagged vs existing_mean_difference (6.605589), single pre-declared candidate
success_rule: Report as improvement candidate only if MAE is lower, the paired person bootstrap 95% range (10000 draws, seed 20261031) is entirely below 0, and at least 4 of 5 outer folds improve. Otherwise report no clear improvement.
limitations: Repeatedly inspected development cohort, not independent confirmation
Inner members are terminal-epoch checkpoints while refit models use inner-selected epochs
Ensemble weights were selected with non-bagged inner predictions
Original study 6.5 used a different evaluation set and is not directly comparable
